title: European Council grants EU candidate status to Ukraine and Moldova
body:
On 23 June 2022, the heads of state and government of the European Union decided to grant EU candidate status to Ukraine and Moldova. European Council President Charles Michel announced the decision on Twitter, writing: "Agreement. EUCO has just decided EU candidate status to Ukraine and Moldova." He called it "a historic moment" and congratulated Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Moldovan President Maia Sandu.

Ukraine's application had been signed by Zelensky on 28 February 2022, four days after the full-scale invasion began. In early April, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen handed Ukraine a questionnaire during a visit to Kyiv, and Ukraine completed and submitted both parts of it. On 17 June 2022 the European Commission published its opinions on the applications from Ukraine, Moldova and Georgia. It recommended candidate status for Ukraine and Moldova and a "European perspective" for Georgia.

Matti Maasikas, head of the EU Delegation to Ukraine, said the decision was "the acknowledgment that Ukraine belongs to the European family" and that work on EU reforms would begin the next day. Candidate status is a step before the opening of accession negotiations and does not itself confer membership. The decision required unanimity among the member states. Accession talks with Ukraine and Moldova were formally opened on 25 June 2024.
